name: Seupa Vapellenentse (Savoy Cabbage Soup)

ingredients.name: hearty rye bread, cut into 1 1/2 to 2-inch pieces
Savoy cabbage, cored and cut into 1-inch pieces

instructions.primary_message: Adjust oven rack to middle position and heat oven to 120°C (250°F). On a rimmed baking sheet, spread bread in an even layer and bake, stirring occasionally, until dried and crisp, 30 to 45 minutes. Let croutons cool completely.
In a Dutch oven or large pot, butter over medium-low until butter is melted. Add lardo or pancetta and cook until browned but still slightly chewy and fat is rendered, 6 to 8 minutes.
Stir in onion and salt and cook over medium heat until softened and lightly browned, 6 to 8 minutes. Stir in garlic and caraway seeds and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add cabbage, broth, and bay leaves and stir to combine. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer until cabbage is tender, 30 to 45 minutes.

Adjust oven rack to 15 cm from upper broiler coils and heat broiler on high. Discard bay leaves and spread half of cabbage mixture evenly in the bottom of a 9-by-33-cm broiler-safe baking dish, then top with half of the croutons. Repeat the layering with the remaining cabbage mixture, topping it with the croutons. Using a wide flat spatula, gently press down on croutons to submerge and saturate. Sprinkle fontina cheese evenly over top. Broil until cheese is melted and spotty brown, 2 to 4 minutes. Sprinkle with parsley and serve.

schema_metadata.keywords: Soueupa alla valpellinentze, Savoy Cabbage Soup, cabbage soup recipe

description: Discover Italy’s coziest Alpine comfort food: seupa vapellenentse. In this deeply savory "soup," braised Savoy cabbage, pancetta, rye bread, and melty fontina come together in layers like a rustic gratin.
notes:
Optional substitutions: lardo → pancetta; homemade beef stock → chicken stock or store-bought low-sodium chicken broth

Notes: In Valle D'Aosta, the bread used is called "pane nero," which means black bread. It's a dense, rustic loaf with a robust rye flavor. Try to get rye loaf like that, and not a lighter Jewish-style rye that is often used in deli sandwiches.

Make-ahead and storage: Leftovers can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat in a 175°C (350°F) oven until warmed through and the bread on top is toasty.
author: Leah Colins
